fact: Africa50 and Bayobab (MTN Group) announced a partnership on 15 May 2023 to co-develop Project East2West, a roughly US$320-325 million terrestrial fibre network linking landlocked countries to east and west coast subsea cables, with Angola among the twelve countries named.

In November 2023 Paratus secured a US$31 million debt facility from EAIF and Ninety One financing a Luanda data centre and three terrestrial fibre routes, one of them Luanda-Lusaka-Dar es Salaam, so Angola, Zambia and Tanzania are named.

fact: ITWeb Africa reports, citing Angola's telecommunications ministry (MINTTICS), that Angola and Mozambique signed a bilateral memorandum in June 2026 under which Mozambique's Tmcel and TVM would use Angola's ANGOSAT-2 satellite for telecom and broadcast signals, with a commercial agreement still to be formalised.

ITWeb Africa reports that Angola's National Space Programme Management Office signed a commercial pilot agreement with Telecom Namibia to validate satellite-driven backhaul; the article gives no signing date, so the document's published date is used.
